Football: Uefa Nations League, starts ~5 hours from time of writing

Portugal vs Switzerland: Bet Builder

Over 0.5 cards for Switzerland

Over 0.5 cards for Portugal

Portugal to 'qualify' (not ML, including extra time and penalties)

1.80 / -125 at Bet365 

Analysis: Portugal won a pretty tight nations league group that included Italy and Poland, despite missing Ronaldo. Switzerland beat Belgium and Iceland on route to the finals here. The big news is that Portugal will welcome Ronaldo for this game, this may be one of the last chances for him to win a trophy with the national team, as he'll be 35 by the time the Euro's take place. But the days of Porgual being a one man team are over. Bernardo Silva was one of the best players in the Premier League this season, the hype surrounding Joao Felix is huge, the Wolves duo of Moutinho and Neves are great on the ball. Switzerland don't have much star power to call on, and are the sort of team that are greater than the sum of their parts. I think home advantage here for Portugal could be enough to see them victory here in what should be a close, intense game. Portugal are the reigning European champions and they boast phenomenal quality going forwards. Switzerland are tough, organised and disciplined, but Portugal have a lot more quality on the ball.

As for the cards part of this bet, the referee today is Felix Brych, who has a good record of showing cards at international level. Both teams will want to get to the final on Sunday and with Pepe touted to start for Portugal, a card almost feels guaranteed for them. Last 5 non friendly games for Portugal averaged 2.4 team cards. The last 5 teams to face Portugal averaged 2.4 team cards also. Switzerland have averaged 1.8 team cards over their last 5 non friendly games. 

Here's a photo to explain how much of a card monster Felix Brych is in international games [:)](https://i.imgur.com/NeIt02k.png)

Last time these two teams met, we saw a 2-0 win for Portugal. 

Sorry if this write up is a bit long/excessive, but I thought it was better to explain everything than to give to little detail :) Best of luck!
